source.text: Διαμαρτύρομαι ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ, τοῦ μέλλοντος κρίνειν ζῶντας καὶ νεκρούς, καὶ τὴν ἐπιφάνειαν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν βασιλείαν αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: I solemnly charge [you] before God and Christ Jesus, the [one] about to judge [the] living and [the] dead, and [by] the appearing of him and the kingdom of him:

en.L: I solemnly charge [you] before God and {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus, who is going to judge the living and the dead, and by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} appearing and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom:
en.B: I solemnly charge you in the presence of God and of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, who will judge the living and the dead, and in view of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} appearing and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom:
en.R: God and {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus are watching. {{christos:Christ|The Messiah}} Jesus will judge everyone, both those who are alive and those who have died. He is coming back, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rule as king. So I give you this serious command:

fr.L: Je [t’]adjure devant Dieu et le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus, qui va juger les vivants et les morts, et par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} apparition et {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} royaume :
fr.B: Devant Dieu et devant le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus, qui jugera les vivants et les morts, et au nom de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} apparition et de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} royaume, je t’en conjure solennellement :
fr.R: Dieu et le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus te regardent. Le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus jugera tout le monde, ceux qui sont vivants et ceux qui sont morts. Il va revenir, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} régnera comme roi. Alors je te donne cet ordre important :

decisions.choice: and by his appearing and his kingdom
decisions.reason: The accusatives are the things by which Paul makes the charge, as one swears by something; his return and reign are the reason to take it seriously.

decisions.choice: his appearing: Christ's return
decisions.reason: In 1:10 ἐπιφάνειαν was his first coming; here, beside judgment and kingdom, it is his return.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: God and {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus are watching
decisions.reason: Readable states what "before God" means.

source.text: κήρυξον τὸν λόγον, ἐπίστηθι εὐκαίρως ἀκαίρως, ἔλεγξον, ἐπιτίμησον, παρακάλεσον, ἐν πάσῃ μακροθυμίᾳ καὶ διδαχῇ.

records.literal_gloss: Preach the word, be ready in season [and] out of season, reprove, rebuke, exhort, with all patience and teaching.

en.L: Preach the word; be ready in season [and] out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort, with complete patience and teaching.
en.B: Preach the word. Be ready whether the time seems right or not. Correct, rebuke and encourage, with great patience and careful teaching.
en.R: Tell people God's message. Be ready to do it at all times, whether it is easy or hard. Show people what they are doing wrong. Warn them, and encourage them. Be very patient with them as you teach them.

fr.L: Proclame la parole ; tiens-toi prêt à temps [et] à contretemps ; reprends, réprimande, exhorte, avec une patience entière et l’enseignement.
fr.B: Proclame la parole. Sois prêt, que le moment semble bon ou non. Corrige, réprimande et encourage, avec une grande patience et un enseignement attentif.
fr.R: Annonce aux gens le message de Dieu. Sois prêt à le faire à tout moment, que ce soit facile ou difficile. Montre aux gens ce qu’ils font de mal. Avertis-les, et encourage-les. Sois très patient avec eux quand tu les enseignes.

decisions.choice: in season and out of season: whether convenient or not
decisions.reason: εὐκαίρως and ἀκαίρως are a play on words: when the moment is right and when it is not.

decisions.choice: the word: the message of the gospel
decisions.reason: As in 2:9 and 2:15.

source.text: ἔσται γὰρ καιρὸς ὅτε τῆς ὑγιαινούσης διδασκαλίας οὐκ ἀνέξονται, ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὰς ἰδίας ἐπιθυμίας ἑαυτοῖς ἐπισωρεύσουσιν διδασκάλους κνηθόμενοι τὴν ἀκοήν, καὶ ἀπὸ μὲν τῆς ἀληθείας τὴν ἀκοὴν ἀποστρέψουσιν, ἐπὶ δὲ τοὺς μύθους ἐκτραπήσονται.

records.literal_gloss: There will be for a time when the sound teaching not they will endure, but according to their own desires for themselves they will heap up teachers having itching the ear, \v 4 and from the truth the hearing they will turn away, to and the myths they will be turned aside.

en.L: For the time will come when they will not put up with sound teaching, but, having itching ears, they will gather around themselves teachers to suit their own desires, \v 4 and they will turn their ears away from the truth and turn aside to myths.
en.B: For a time will come when people will not put up with sound teaching. Instead, wanting to hear what their ears itch for, they will gather around them a great number of teachers to suit their own desires. \v 4 They will turn away from listening to the truth and wander off into myths.
en.R: A time will come when people will not want to listen to the true teaching. They will find many teachers who will tell them only what they want to hear, because they want to do whatever they like. \v 4 They will stop listening to the truth, and they will start to believe stories that people have made up.

fr.L: Car il y aura un temps où ils ne supporteront pas l’enseignement sain, mais, ayant l’oreille qui leur démange, ils accumuleront pour eux-mêmes des enseignants selon leurs propres désirs, \v 4 et ils détourneront l’oreille de la vérité et se tourneront vers les mythes.
fr.B: Car un temps viendra où les gens ne supporteront plus l’enseignement sain. Au contraire, avides d’entendre ce qui flatte leurs oreilles, ils s’entoureront d’une foule d’enseignants à la mesure de leurs propres désirs. \v 4 Ils cesseront d’écouter la vérité et se laisseront aller vers des mythes.
fr.R: Un jour viendra où les gens ne voudront plus écouter le véritable enseignement. Ils chercheront beaucoup d’enseignants qui leur diront seulement ce qu’ils ont envie d’entendre, parce qu’ils veulent faire tout ce qui leur plaît. \v 4 Ils arrêteront d’écouter la vérité, et ils se mettront à croire des histoires que des gens ont inventées.

decisions.choice: itching ears: wanting to hear something pleasing
decisions.reason: κνηθόμενοι is to have an itch: they want their ears tickled with what they like to hear.

decisions.choice: heap up: gather a great number
decisions.reason: ἐπισωρεύω is to pile up: they collect teacher after teacher.

decisions.choice: myths: stories without truth
decisions.reason: As in 1 Timothy 1:4 and 4:7.

source.text: σὺ δὲ νῆφε ἐν πᾶσιν, κακοπάθησον, ἔργον ποίησον εὐαγγελιστοῦ, τὴν διακονίαν σου πληροφόρησον.

records.literal_gloss: You but be sober in all things, suffer hardship, [the] work do of an evangelist, the ministry of you fully carry out.

en.L: But as for you, be sober-minded in all things, endure hardship, do the work of an evangelist, fulfill your ministry.
en.B: But you, keep a clear head in every situation. Endure hardship, do the work of an evangelist, and carry out your ministry fully.
en.R: But you must think clearly at all times. Be ready to suffer. Keep telling people the good news. Do everything God has given you to do.

fr.L: Mais toi, sois sobre en toutes choses, supporte la souffrance, fais l’œuvre d’un évangéliste, accomplis pleinement ton ministère.
fr.B: Mais toi, garde l’esprit clair en toute situation. Supporte la souffrance, fais le travail d’un évangéliste, et accomplis pleinement ton ministère.
fr.R: Mais toi, tu dois avoir les idées claires à tout moment. Sois prêt à souffrir. Continue d’annoncer la bonne nouvelle aux gens. Fais tout ce que Dieu t’a donné à faire.

decisions.choice: be sober-minded: be clear-headed and watchful
decisions.reason: νήφω is literally to be sober; here, to keep a clear mind, unlike those carried away by myths (verse 4).

decisions.choice: an evangelist: one who proclaims the good news
decisions.reason: εὐαγγελιστοῦ is one who brings the gospel to others (Acts 21:8; Ephesians 4:11).

decisions.choice: Keep telling people the good news
alternatives: do the work of an evangelist
decisions.reason: Readable explains the title (m2).

decisions.choice: sois sobre (L); garde l’esprit clair (B); avoir les idées claires (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of sobriety; Balanced and Readable say the sense, clear-headed and watchful (m1), since French "sobre" today mostly means abstaining from drink or plain in style.

source.text: Ἐγὼ γὰρ ἤδη σπένδομαι, καὶ ὁ καιρὸς τῆς ἀναλύσεώς μου ἐφέστηκεν.

records.literal_gloss: I for already am being poured out as a drink offering, and the time of the departure of me has come.

en.L: For I am already being poured out as a drink offering, and the time of my departure has come.
en.B: For I am already being poured out like a drink offering, and the time for my departure has come.
en.R: My life is already being poured out like an offering to God. The time has come for me to leave this life.

fr.L: Car moi, je suis déjà versé en libation, et le temps de mon départ est arrivé.
fr.B: Car déjà ma vie est répandue comme une libation, et le moment de mon départ est venu.
fr.R: Ma vie est déjà en train d’être versée comme une offrande à Dieu. Le moment est venu pour moi de quitter cette vie.

decisions.choice: poured out as a drink offering
decisions.reason: σπένδομαι is to pour out a drink offering of wine, which accompanied sacrifices (Numbers 15:1-10). Paul sees his coming death as an offering to God (Philippians 2:17).

decisions.choice: my departure: my death
decisions.reason: ἀναλύσεώς is the loosing of a ship from its moorings or the striking of a tent: leaving this life.

decisions.choice: to leave this life
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that Paul means his death (m2).

decisions.choice: versé en libation (L); répandue comme une libation (B)
decisions.reason: "Libation" is the French word for an offering of wine poured out (m1), and keeps the picture of the verb; Readable says "une offrande à Dieu", as the English says "an offering to God".

source.text: τὸν καλὸν ἀγῶνα ἠγώνισμαι, τὸν δρόμον τετέλεκα, τὴν πίστιν τετήρηκα·

records.literal_gloss: The good fight I have fought, the race I have finished, the faith I have kept;

en.L: I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.
en.B: I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.
en.R: I have struggled hard in the contest, like an athlete. I have run the whole race. I have kept my faith.

fr.L: Le beau combat, je l’ai combattu ; la course, je l’ai achevée ; la foi, je l’ai gardée.
fr.B: J’ai livré le bon combat, j’ai fini la course, j’ai gardé la foi.
fr.R: J’ai lutté de toutes mes forces dans la compétition, comme un athlète. J’ai couru toute la course. J’ai gardé ma foi.

decisions.choice: the good fight: the athlete's contest
decisions.reason: ἀγῶνα is any contest, especially in the games, as is the race that follows; compare 1 Timothy 6:12.

decisions.choice: kept the faith: stayed faithful, guarded the truth
alternatives: kept faith, as one keeps a promise
decisions.reason: τὴν πίστιν may be the Christian faith guarded (1:14) or Paul's own loyalty, as one keeps faith with a promise. Both are true of Paul.

decisions.choice: struggled hard in the contest, like an athlete
decisions.reason: Readable states the picture (m1).

decisions.choice: "Le beau combat, je l’ai combattu ; la course, je l’ai achevée ; la foi, je l’ai gardée" (L)
alternatives: "J’ai combattu le bon combat, j’ai achevé la course, j’ai gardé la foi"
decisions.reason: The Greek puts each object first; French can keep that order with a resumed pronoun, so Literal shows the emphasis, which also falls on the noble contest of an athlete (m1). Balanced uses the ordinary order.

source.text: λοιπὸν ἀπόκειταί μοι ὁ τῆς δικαιοσύνης στέφανος, ὃν ἀποδώσει μοι ὁ κύριος ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ, ὁ δίκαιος κριτής, οὐ μόνον δὲ ἐμοὶ ἀλλὰ καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ἠγαπηκόσι τὴν ἐπιφάνειαν αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: from now on is laid up for me the of righteousness crown, which will award to me the Lord in that day, the righteous judge, not only but to me but also to all those having loved the appearing of him.

en.L: Henceforth the crown of righteousness is laid up for me, which the Lord, the righteous judge, will award to me on that day, and not only to me but also to all who have loved {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} appearing.
en.B: Now there is waiting for me the crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, will give me on that day, and not only to me but also to all who have longed for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} appearing.
en.R: Now there is a prize waiting for me, the crown of righteousness. The Lord is a righteous judge, and on the day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes back {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give me this prize. He will give it not only to me but to everyone who has looked forward with love to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} coming.

fr.L: Désormais m’est réservée la couronne de justice, que le Seigneur, le juste juge, me remettra en ce jour-là, et non seulement à moi, mais aussi à tous ceux qui ont aimé {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} apparition.
fr.B: Désormais, la couronne de justice m’attend. Le Seigneur, le juste juge, me la donnera en ce jour-là, et pas seulement à moi, mais aussi à tous ceux qui ont ardemment désiré {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} apparition.
fr.R: Maintenant, un prix m’attend : la couronne de justice. Le Seigneur est un juge juste, et le jour où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} reviendra, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me donnera ce prix. Il ne le donnera pas seulement à moi, mais à tous ceux qui ont attendu {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} retour avec amour.

decisions.choice: the crown of righteousness: the crown that is righteousness, or that rewards it
alternatives: the crown given to the righteous
decisions.reason: The genitive may mean the crown which consists of righteousness (final vindication) or the reward for a righteous life. Both fit the picture of the righteous judge.

decisions.choice: the crown: the victor's wreath
decisions.reason: στέφανος is the wreath given to the winner of a contest (2:5), not a royal crown.

decisions.choice: longed for
decisions.reason: Those who "love his appearing" are those who long for his return.

source.text: Σπούδασον ἐλθεῖν πρός με ταχέως·

records.literal_gloss: Make every effort to come to me quickly;

en.L: Do your best to come to me quickly.
en.B: Do your best to come to me soon.
en.R: Try hard to come to me soon.

fr.L: Efforce-toi de venir auprès de moi rapidement.
fr.B: Fais ton possible pour venir me rejoindre bientôt.
fr.R: Essaie vraiment de venir me voir bientôt.

decisions.choice: do your best
decisions.reason: σπουδάζω is to make haste, to be eager, as in 2:15 and 4:21.

source.text: Δημᾶς γάρ με ἐγκατέλιπεν ἀγαπήσας τὸν νῦν αἰῶνα, καὶ ἐπορεύθη εἰς Θεσσαλονίκην, Κρήσκης εἰς Γαλατίαν, Τίτος εἰς Δαλματίαν·

records.literal_gloss: Demas for me has deserted, having loved the present age, and has gone to Thessalonica, Crescens to Galatia, Titus to Dalmatia;

en.L: For Demas has deserted me, having loved the present age, and has gone to Thessalonica; Crescens [has gone] to Galatia, Titus to Dalmatia.
en.B: Demas, in love with this present world, has deserted me and gone to Thessalonica. Crescens has gone to Galatia and Titus to Dalmatia.
en.R: Demas loved the things of this world too much, so he left me and went to Thessalonica. Crescens has gone to Galatia, and Titus has gone to Dalmatia.

fr.L: Car Démas m’a abandonné, ayant aimé l’âge présent, et il est parti pour Thessalonique ; Crescens [est parti] pour la Galatie, Tite pour la Dalmatie.
fr.B: Démas, par amour pour le monde présent, m’a abandonné et il est parti pour Thessalonique. Crescens est allé en Galatie, et Tite en Dalmatie.
fr.R: Démas a trop aimé les choses de ce monde, alors il m’a quitté et il est parti à Thessalonique. Crescens est allé en Galatie, et Tite est allé en Dalmatie.

decisions.choice: Demas
decisions.reason: Demas was with Paul in his earlier imprisonment (Colossians 4:14; Philemon 24).

decisions.choice: the present age: this world and its life
decisions.reason: αἰῶνα is an age; "the present age" is the world as it now is, set against the coming one.

decisions.choice: Galatia, Dalmatia
decisions.reason: Galatia was in central Asia Minor (some manuscripts read "Gaul"); Dalmatia is on the eastern Adriatic coast (modern Croatia). Crescens and Titus seem to have gone on mission, not deserted.

decisions.choice: this present world (B); this world (R)
decisions.reason: The sense is this world and its life (m2).

source.text: Λουκᾶς ἐστιν μόνος μετ’ ἐμοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Luke is alone with me.

en.L: Only Luke is with me.
en.B: Only Luke is with me.
en.R: Only Luke is with me now.

fr.L: Luc seul est avec moi.
fr.B: Seul Luc est avec moi.
fr.R: Il n’y a que Luc avec moi maintenant.

decisions.choice: Luke: the doctor
decisions.reason: Luke, "the beloved physician" (Colossians 4:14), traveled with Paul (Acts 16:10, 27:1).

source.text: Μᾶρκον ἀναλαβὼν ἄγε μετὰ σεαυτοῦ, ἔστιν γάρ μοι εὔχρηστος εἰς διακονίαν, Τυχικὸν δὲ ἀπέστειλα εἰς Ἔφεσον.

records.literal_gloss: Mark having taken bring with yourself, he is for to me useful for ministry. \v 12 Tychicus but I sent to Ephesus.

en.L: Get Mark and bring him with you, for he is useful to me for ministry. \v 12 But Tychicus I have sent to Ephesus.
en.B: Get Mark and bring him with you, because he is helpful to me in my work. \v 12 I have sent Tychicus to Ephesus.
en.R: Find Mark and bring him with you. He can help me in my work. \v 12 I have sent Tychicus to Ephesus.

fr.L: Prends Marc et amène-le avec toi, car il m’est utile pour le service. \v 12 Mais Tychique, je l’ai envoyé à Éphèse.
fr.B: Va chercher Marc et amène-le avec toi, car il m’est d’une grande aide dans mon travail. \v 12 J’ai envoyé Tychique à Éphèse.
fr.R: Trouve Marc et amène-le avec toi. Il peut m’aider dans mon travail. \v 12 J’ai envoyé Tychique à Éphèse.

decisions.choice: Mark: once a cause of division, now useful
decisions.reason: John Mark left Paul on his first journey, and Paul refused to take him again (Acts 13:13, 15:37-39). Later Mark was with Paul again (Colossians 4:10; Philemon 24).

decisions.choice: ministry: service, either to Paul or in the gospel
decisions.reason: διακονίαν may be personal help to Paul or service in the work of the gospel.

decisions.choice: Tychicus
decisions.reason: Tychicus was Paul's trusted messenger (Ephesians 6:21; Colossians 4:7). He may have carried this letter, and replaced Timothy in Ephesus.

source.text: τὸν φαιλόνην, ὃν ἀπέλιπον ἐν Τρῳάδι παρὰ Κάρπῳ, ἐρχόμενος φέρε, καὶ τὰ βιβλία, μάλιστα τὰς μεμβράνας.

records.literal_gloss: The cloak which I left in Troas with Carpus, coming bring, and the books, especially the parchments.

en.L: When you come, bring the cloak that I left in Troas with Carpus, and the books, especially the parchments.
en.B: When you come, bring the cloak I left with Carpus at Troas, and my scrolls, especially the parchments.
en.R: When you come, bring the coat that I left with Carpus in Troas. Also bring my books, especially the ones written on parchment.

fr.L: Quand tu viendras, apporte le manteau que j’ai laissé à Troas chez Carpus, et les livres, surtout les parchemins.
fr.B: Quand tu viendras, apporte le manteau que j’ai laissé chez Carpus à Troas, ainsi que mes rouleaux, surtout les parchemins.
fr.R: Quand tu viendras, apporte le manteau que j’ai laissé chez Carpus, à Troas. Apporte aussi mes livres, surtout ceux qui sont écrits sur du parchemin.

decisions.choice: the cloak: a heavy outer garment
decisions.reason: φαιλόνην is a heavy, sleeveless cape, needed in a prison as winter came (verse 21).

decisions.choice: the books and the parchments
decisions.reason: βιβλία are scrolls, probably papyrus. μεμβράνας are sheets of parchment (prepared animal skin), perhaps notebooks or copies of the Scriptures. We do not know their contents.

source.text: Ἀλέξανδρος ὁ χαλκεὺς πολλά μοι κακὰ ἐνεδείξατο ἀποδώσει αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ ὃν καὶ σὺ φυλάσσου, λίαν γὰρ ἀντέστη τοῖς ἡμετέροις λόγοις.

records.literal_gloss: Alexander the coppersmith many to me evils did; will repay him the Lord according to the deeds of him; \v 15 whom also you guard against, greatly for he opposed our words.

en.L: Alexander the coppersmith did me much harm; the Lord will repay him according to his deeds. \v 15 You also beware of him, for he strongly opposed our words.
en.B: Alexander the metalworker did me a great deal of harm. The Lord will repay him for what he has done. \v 15 You too should be on guard against him, because he strongly opposed our message.
en.R: Alexander, who works with metal, did many bad things to me. The Lord will punish him for what he has done. \v 15 You must be careful of him too, because he fought hard against what we teach.

fr.L: Alexandre le chaudronnier m’a fait beaucoup de mal ; le Seigneur lui rendra selon ses œuvres. \v 15 Toi aussi, garde-toi de lui, car il s’est violemment opposé à nos paroles.
fr.B: Alexandre, l’artisan du métal, m’a fait beaucoup de mal. Le Seigneur lui rendra ce qu’il a fait. \v 15 Toi aussi, méfie-toi de lui, car il s’est fortement opposé à notre message.
fr.R: Alexandre, qui travaille le métal, m’a fait beaucoup de mal. Le Seigneur le punira pour ce qu’il a fait. \v 15 Fais attention à lui, toi aussi, car il a lutté de toutes ses forces contre ce que nous enseignons.

decisions.choice: Alexander the coppersmith
decisions.reason: Perhaps the Alexander of 1 Timothy 1:20, or of Acts 19:33; the name was common. χαλκεὺς is a smith in copper or bronze, or any metalworker.

decisions.choice: the Lord will repay him according to his deeds
decisions.reason: The words echo Psalm 62:13 and Proverbs 24:12. Some manuscripts have the wish "may the Lord repay"; the SBLGNT has the future.

decisions.choice: our words: our message
decisions.reason: λόγοις is plural: Paul's preaching, or his defense at his trial.

source.text: Ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ μου ἀπολογίᾳ οὐδείς μοι παρεγένετο, ἀλλὰ πάντες με ἐγκατέλιπον μὴ αὐτοῖς λογισθείη ὁ δὲ κύριός μοι παρέστη καὶ ἐνεδυνάμωσέν με, ἵνα δι’ ἐμοῦ τὸ κήρυγμα πληροφορηθῇ καὶ ἀκούσωσιν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, καὶ ἐρρύσθην ἐκ στόματος λέοντος.

records.literal_gloss: At the first of me defense no one me stood by, but all me deserted; not to them may it be counted; \v 17 the but Lord me stood by and strengthened me, so that through me the proclamation might be fully carried out and might hear all the Gentiles, and I was rescued out of [the] mouth of a lion.

en.L: At my first defense no one stood by me, but all deserted me. May it not be counted against them. \v 17 But the Lord stood by me and strengthened me, so that through me the proclamation might be fully carried out and all the Gentiles might hear [it]; and I was rescued from the lion's mouth.
en.B: At my first defense no one came to support me; everyone deserted me. May it not be held against them. \v 17 But the Lord stood by me and gave me strength, so that through me the message might be fully proclaimed and all the Gentiles might hear it. And I was rescued from the lion's mouth.
en.R: The first time I had to defend myself in court, no one came to help me. They all left me alone. I pray that God will not hold it against them. \v 17 But the Lord stayed with me and made me strong. He did this so that I could tell the whole message, and all the Gentiles could hear it. And the Lord saved me from great danger, as if from the mouth of a lion.

fr.L: Lors de ma première défense, personne ne s’est tenu à mes côtés, mais tous m’ont abandonné. Que cela ne leur soit pas compté ! \v 17 Mais le Seigneur s’est tenu à mes côtés et m’a fortifié, afin que par moi la proclamation soit pleinement accomplie et que toutes les nations [l’]entendent ; et j’ai été délivré de la gueule du lion.
fr.B: Lors de ma première défense, personne n’est venu me soutenir ; tous m’ont abandonné. Que cela ne soit pas retenu contre eux ! \v 17 Mais le Seigneur s’est tenu près de moi et m’a donné de la force, afin que par moi le message soit pleinement proclamé et que tous les non-Juifs l’entendent. Et j’ai été arraché à la gueule du lion.
fr.R: La première fois que j’ai dû me défendre au tribunal, personne n’est venu m’aider. Ils m’ont tous laissé seul. Je prie pour que Dieu ne le leur reproche pas. \v 17 Mais le Seigneur est resté avec moi et m’a rendu fort. Il l’a fait pour que je puisse annoncer tout le message, et que tous les non-Juifs puissent l’entendre. Et le Seigneur m’a sauvé d’un grand danger, comme s’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’avait tiré de la gueule d’un lion.

decisions.choice: my first defense: the first hearing of Paul's trial
alternatives: his defense at an earlier imprisonment
decisions.reason: A Roman trial could have a preliminary hearing. Paul speaks of it as recent, so it is probably the first stage of his present trial.

decisions.choice: the lion's mouth: deadly danger
decisions.reason: The phrase recalls Psalm 22:22 and Daniel 6. It is a picture of mortal danger; some have seen a reference to Nero or to the arena, but as a Roman citizen Paul would not be thrown to the lions.

decisions.choice: may it not be counted against them
decisions.reason: Like Jesus (Luke 23:34) and Stephen (Acts 7:60), Paul forgives those who failed him.

decisions.choice: saved me from great danger, as if from the mouth of a lion
decisions.reason: Readable states the picture (m2).

decisions.choice: les nations (L); les non-Juifs (B, R) (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: As in Colossians and the style guide (§9): "les Gentils" is no longer current French and "les païens" sounds pejorative; Balanced and Readable say "non-Juifs" where the English says "Gentiles".

source.text: ῥύσεταί με ὁ κύριος ἀπὸ παντὸς ἔργου πονηροῦ καὶ σώσει εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν αὐτοῦ τὴν ἐπουράνιον· ᾧ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, ἀμήν.

records.literal_gloss: Will rescue me the Lord from every work evil and will save into the kingdom of him the heavenly; to whom [be] the glory to the ages of the ages, amen.

en.L: The Lord will rescue me from every evil deed and will bring [me] safely into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} heavenly kingdom. To {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [be] the glory for ever and ever. Amen.
en.B: The Lord will rescue me from every evil attack and bring me safely into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} heavenly kingdom. To {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} be the glory for ever and ever. Amen.
en.R: The Lord will save me from every evil thing that people try to do to me, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bring me safely into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom in heaven. Give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} glory for ever and ever. Amen.

fr.L: Le Seigneur me délivrera de toute œuvre mauvaise et [me] mènera sain et sauf dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} royaume céleste. À {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} la gloire pour les siècles des siècles. Amen.
fr.B: Le Seigneur me délivrera de toute attaque du mal et me fera parvenir sain et sauf dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} royaume céleste. À {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} soit la gloire pour toujours et à jamais ! Amen.
fr.R: Le Seigneur me sauvera de tout le mal que les gens essaient de me faire, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me conduira en sécurité dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} royaume, au ciel. Gloire à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} pour toujours et à jamais ! Amen.

decisions.choice: will bring me safely into his kingdom
decisions.reason: σώσει is the verb "save", here meaning to bring safe through to the end. Paul does not expect rescue from death (verse 6) but rescue through it.

decisions.choice: for ever and ever
decisions.reason: Literally "to the ages of the ages", an idiom for eternity.

decisions.choice: bring [me] safely (L); bring me safely (B, R)
decisions.reason: The sense is safe arrival (m1), so the key term "save" is not used for this word.

decisions.choice: mènera sain et sauf (L); fera parvenir sain et sauf (B)
decisions.reason: As in English, the sense is a safe arrival (m1), so "sauver" is not used here; "sain et sauf" says it in ordinary French.

source.text: Ἄσπασαι Πρίσκαν καὶ Ἀκύλαν καὶ τὸν Ὀνησιφόρου οἶκον.

records.literal_gloss: Greet Prisca and Aquila and the of Onesiphorus household.

en.L: Greet Prisca and Aquila and the household of Onesiphorus.
en.B: Greet Prisca and Aquila and the household of Onesiphorus.
en.R: Say hello to Prisca and Aquila and to the family of Onesiphorus.

fr.L: Salue Prisca et Aquilas et la maison d’Onésiphore.
fr.B: Salue Prisca et Aquilas, ainsi que la famille d’Onésiphore.
fr.R: Dis bonjour de ma part à Prisca et Aquilas, et à la famille d’Onésiphore.

decisions.choice: Prisca and Aquila
decisions.reason: A married couple, tentmakers like Paul, who worked with him in Corinth and Ephesus (Acts 18:2-3, 18:26). Prisca is the Priscilla of Acts; she is often named first.

decisions.choice: the household of Onesiphorus

source.text: Ἔραστος ἔμεινεν ἐν Κορίνθῳ, Τρόφιμον δὲ ἀπέλιπον ἐν Μιλήτῳ ἀσθενοῦντα.

records.literal_gloss: Erastus remained in Corinth, Trophimus but I left in Miletus being sick.

en.L: Erastus remained in Corinth, but Trophimus I left sick in Miletus.
en.B: Erastus stayed in Corinth, and I left Trophimus sick in Miletus.
en.R: Erastus stayed in Corinth. Trophimus was sick, so I left him in Miletus.

fr.L: Éraste est resté à Corinthe, et Trophime, je l’ai laissé malade à Milet.
fr.B: Éraste est resté à Corinthe, et j’ai laissé Trophime malade à Milet.
fr.R: Éraste est resté à Corinthe. Trophime était malade, alors je l’ai laissé à Milet.

decisions.choice: Erastus and Trophimus
decisions.reason: Erastus may be the city official of Corinth (Romans 16:23) or Paul's helper (Acts 19:22). Trophimus was from Ephesus (Acts 20:4, 21:29). Miletus is a port south of Ephesus.

source.text: Σπούδασον πρὸ χειμῶνος ἐλθεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: Make every effort before winter to come.

en.L: Do your best to come before winter.
en.B: Do your best to get here before winter.
en.R: Try hard to come before winter.

fr.L: Efforce-toi de venir avant l’hiver.
fr.B: Fais ton possible pour arriver avant l’hiver.
fr.R: Essaie vraiment de venir avant l’hiver.

decisions.choice: before winter
decisions.reason: Ships stopped sailing in winter (Acts 27:9-12); if Timothy waited, he could not come until spring.

source.text: Ἀσπάζεταί σε Εὔβουλος καὶ Πούδης καὶ Λίνος καὶ Κλαυδία καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ πάντες.

records.literal_gloss: Greets you Eubulus and Pudens and Linus and Claudia and the brothers all.

en.L: Eubulus greets you, and Pudens and Linus and Claudia and all the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.
en.B: Eubulus sends you greetings, as do Pudens, Linus, Claudia and all the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.
en.R: Eubulus says hello to you. So do Pudens, Linus, Claudia and all the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} here.

fr.L: Eubulus te salue, et Pudens et Linus et Claudia et tous les {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}.
fr.B: Eubulus te salue, ainsi que Pudens, Linus, Claudia et tous les {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}.
fr.R: Eubulus te dit bonjour. Pudens, Linus, Claudia et tous les {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} d’ici te saluent aussi.

decisions.choice: Eubulus, Pudens, Linus, Claudia
decisions.reason: Believers in Rome; Claudia is a woman. Irenaeus names a Linus as an early leader of the church in Rome.

decisions.choice: the brothers: fellow believers, men and women
decisions.reason: ἀδελφοὶ was used for all believers in a church.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is to the whole church, women and men; "brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}
decisions.reason: As in English and Colossians, fellow believers, men and women, are meant (m2); "frères" stays available as the traditional form.

source.text: Ὁ κύριος μετὰ τοῦ πνεύματός σου.

records.literal_gloss: The Lord [be] with the spirit of you.

en.L: The Lord [be] with your spirit.
en.B: The Lord be with your spirit.
en.R: I pray that the Lord will be with you.

fr.L: [Que] le Seigneur [soit] avec ton esprit.
fr.B: Que le Seigneur soit avec ton esprit.
fr.R: Je prie pour que le Seigneur soit avec toi.

decisions.choice: your: singular, to Timothy
decisions.reason: σου is singular; the final blessing (s2) is plural.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "the Lord"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "the Lord Jesus Christ" or "the Lord Jesus".

source.text: ἡ χάρις μεθ’ ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: The grace [be] with you all.

en.L: Grace [be] with you [all].
en.B: Grace be with you all.
en.R: I pray that God will show grace to all of you.

fr.L: [Que] la grâce [soit] avec vous.
fr.B: Que la grâce soit avec vous tous.
fr.R: Je prie pour que Dieu vous montre {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grâce, à vous tous.

decisions.choice: you: plural, to the church with Timothy
decisions.reason: ὑμῶν is plural: the letter is personal, but read in the church.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: no "Amen"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "Amen".

decisions.choice: [all] (L); all (B); all of you (R)
decisions.reason: English "you" does not show the plural (m1).

decisions.choice: "avec vous" (L), with no "[tous]"
decisions.reason: French "vous" after the "ton" of the previous sentence already shows the change to the plural (m1), which the English Literal has to supply with "[all]".
